title: PortEmailV1
description: K-12 v1, the email port (Resend) in Rosie's own terms (02-contracts K-12): send one email row; verify and parse a webhook (a delivery event, or the notice that a reply came in); read an inbound reply into one K-06 event; and the email double's test hooks (a signed webhook, and the emails it recorded, for the test-phone page). Each call's request, response and errors are definitions under $defs named <call>.request, <call>.response and <call>.errors (02-contracts section 2 item 2), and <call>.exchange pairs one request with its outcome, which is what every fixture is. The root is any one exchange, so the type generator writes a type for every call (ADR-005). Resend's wire format (its paths, headers, field names and codes) stays inside the adapter, with recorded vendor samples beside this contract in vendor-samples/ (02-contracts section 5); the README records what the spike found in Resend's documents. Keys are named, never shown (rule 7): sendEmail reads RESEND_API_KEY, verifyWebhook RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET and readReply RESEND_RECEIVING_KEY from the environment, and no request or response holds any of them. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here.

id.title: Id
id.description: An opaque id code compares as a whole and never parses (CQ-09). Resend's own ids (an email's id, a received email's id, an attachment's id) are UUIDs, and a webhook's id is Svix's msg_ form (README 'Spike findings'); fixtures use readable placeholders, as K-06 and K-07 do.

utc.title: Utc
utc.description: An instant in UTC (CQ-09). The adapter writes Resend's ISO 8601 times to whole seconds, as K-06's and K-07's fixtures write them (README default 8).

emailAddress.title: EmailAddress
emailAddress.description: An email address in lower case, as K-04's handles.address writes an email handle (K-04 handles_address_form; K-06 handle). The adapter takes the bare address from Resend's fields and lowers it (README 'Spike findings': a received email's from is the bare address).

rfcMessageId.title: RfcMessageId
rfcMessageId.description: An email's Message-ID header value as RFC 5322 writes it, angle brackets included, such as <111-222-333@email.example.com>: Resend sets it on every email it sends and reports it as message_id on its email webhooks; a reply's own is in the received email's message_id (README 'Spike findings'). The thread headers name earlier emails by it.

partKey.title: PartKey
partKey.description: The email part's idempotency key, '<row>/<part>/<try>', K-07 v1's (arch 01 line 65; an email row has one part: K-07 'Email rows'). Sent as Resend's Idempotency-Key header: within 24 hours a repeat with the same key and the same email answers the first answer and sends nothing again (README 'Spike findings').

given.title: Given
given.description: What a fixture assumes before the call: the moment it runs, a note, and for a webhook how it was signed. Fixtures only; never sent.

signing.description: For a webhook: how its signature header was made. valid: Svix's HMAC-SHA256 over '<webhookId>.<timestamp>.<raw>' under the test environment's signing secret (the email double's, C-213), base64, written 'v1,<signature>'; oneByteChanged: that signature with one byte changed. The fixture holds no secret and no real signature (rule 7): the contract test signs the fixture's own webhook id, timestamp and raw body at run time and, for oneByteChanged, changes one byte (README 'Fixtures').

purpose.title: EmailPurpose
purpose.description: Why this email goes: the transactional uses 02-contracts K-12 lists, and nothing else, so a marketing email has no purpose it can carry (RULES 4.1: 'Email is transactional only, never marketing'; RULES 4.4: no offers, news, invites or 'book again'). confirmation: a booking's confirmation that carries the chat link and its QR, for a mobile whose chat is not open (MC C9; RULES 4.1b; 'Never opened: each new booking's confirmation carries the link again'). copy: the copy of a message to a customer who gave an email (RULES 4.1: 'A customer's email gets every message, in step with the chat'; arch 02 line 125; K-07 copyOfRowId). emailWay: a message to a person whose way is email (RULES 4.8; arch 02 line 125: 'email only for the email way'), such as an owner after a STOP (S1-10: the owner email 'is where Rosie writes if the owner texts STOP'). nextWay: the next way after texts kept failing for 15 minutes (S12-09, S12-10; arch 02 line 125; K-07 followUps nextWay), to a customer or to the owner. code: a proof code (RULES 6.1, 6.2; MC C9; FS row B13; S1-75; K-09 sendProofCode). notice: S1-35's go-live notice to the listing's email (Q-02's default: 'Notice: email only').

sender.title: EmailSender
sender.description: The From of every email: the one confirmation address, showing the business name (RULES 4.1: 'One email address for every confirmation. It shows the business name.'), on mail.rosfield.com, the sending domain Resend verified (DL-028; SPF, DKIM and DMARC set: RULES 4.1).

name.description: The name the From shows: the business's display name for an email about one business (K-04 businesses.display_name, B02: with the sensitive switch on, only it shows: RULES 4.6), else 'Rosie' (README default 3). One line, with no angle brackets or double quotes, since the adapter writes it as 'name <address>'.

address.description: The one confirmation address, a config value the adapter holds (README default 2), on mail.rosfield.com (DL-028).

chatLink.title: EmailChatLink
chatLink.description: The chat link a confirmation carries, with its QR (MC C9: 'The chat link, with a QR code beside it wherever a screen shows it, reaches the person through ... the booking page and the confirmation email'): K-09's issueChatLink outcome as it gave it, given via confirmation_email (K-29 chat_links.given_via). The text holds the link; the adapter draws the QR from qrText as an attached image, since a plain-text email shows none inline (README default 5).

link.description: The link that opens Messages to Rosie's number with the ready text (K-09 issueChatLink link; RULES 4.1b).

readyText.description: The ready text the link fills in, with its short code: for a booking, 'Hey, send me further updates about my booking' and a short booking ref (RULES 4.1b; K-29 chat_links.ready_text).

shortCode.description: The link's short code, which the ready text holds (K-29 chat_links.short_code; MC C9).

qrText.description: The text the QR code encodes (K-09 issueChatLink qrText).

thread.title: EmailThread
thread.description: The headers that keep an email in the booking's reply thread (02-contracts K-12; RULES 4.1: 'Rosie answers replies in that thread'): In-Reply-To and References, which Resend documents as custom headers for threading (README 'Spike findings'). The first email of a booking's thread, and an email about no booking, has none.

inReplyTo.description: The Message-ID this email answers: a person's reply (K-06 messageId of the email text event), or Rosie's last email in the thread (as its receipt reported it: verifyWebhook rfcMessageId); null for none.

references.description: The Message-IDs of the thread's earlier emails, oldest first, the last of them inReplyTo (RFC 5322 References; Resend: 'append the previous message_ids to the References header'); empty for none.

sendEmail.request.title: SendEmailRequest
sendEmail.request.description: Send one email row (02-contracts K-12 'Send one email row'; arch 07 line 371: 'Email is its own row with the same plan, the automated-assistant line (RULES 1.11), a code-built subject like S12-10's, typed options and a manage link, in the booking's reply thread'): one email to one person, plain text, under its K-07 key. The runtime's email rows (C-129) build it from the row's final parts (K-03, the options typed: K-07 'Email rows') and add what K-07 v1's final parts carry none of (K-07 open gap 7): the subject, the automated-assistant line, the manage link and the thread. text holds every word as it goes; assistantLine, manageLink and chatLink name what it must hold, so the double, the contract test and the checks can find each (README 'The email row').

bookingId.description: The booking it is about (K-04 bookings.id), whose own reply address and manage link it carries; null for an email about no booking, such as a sign-in code or S12-10's notice to the owner.

to.description: The one person it goes to: their email handle's address (K-04 handles.address; RULES 4.8: 'an email if they have one'). Staging sends only to the few named inboxes (Q-23's default), by the adapter's allow-list, not a field here.

replyTo.description: The booking's own reply address (RULES 4.1: 'Each booking has its own reply address, and Rosie answers replies in that thread'; K-04 threads.reply_address of the booking's email thread), sent as Reply-To so a reply comes back to it; null only for an email about no booking. Its domain is the receiving domain J-14 decides (README open gap 1).

subject.description: The subject, built by code, never written by the model (arch 07 line 371: 'a code-built subject like S12-10's', such as 'Booked: Sat Nov 7, 2:00pm'). One line: a line break is refused, so no header can be added through it.

text.description: The whole plain-text body as it goes (02-contracts K-12: 'the plain text with typed options and a manage link'): the automated-assistant line first, then the row's final words with any options typed (K-07 'Email rows'; arch 07 line 371), then the manage link, and for a confirmation the chat link. No HTML part in v1.

assistantLine.description: The fixed line that says Rosie is an automated assistant, word for word as code adds it (RULES 1.11: 'Rosie says it is an automated assistant in every call, chat and email'; arch 07 line 361's opener, 'This is Rosie, the automated booking assistant for <business>.'). The text's first line; one line, and it says 'automated'.

manageLink.description: The secure link to manage the booking, which the text holds (arch 07 line 371: 'a manage link'; S12-10: 'Manage your booking: rosfield.com/m/b07'); null for an email about no booking. Its host is a config value (Q-51).

chatLink.description: For a confirmation, the chat link and its QR (MC C9); null for every other purpose.

bookingId.description: An email about a booking carries the booking's reply address and its manage link (RULES 4.1; arch 07 line 371); one about no booking has neither and no thread, since an email thread belongs to one booking (K-04 threads_chat_or_email).

purpose.description: What each purpose carries (MC C9; RULES 4.1, 4.1b).

then.description: A confirmation is about its booking and carries the chat link and QR (MC C9).

else.description: Only a confirmation carries the chat link (MC C9: 'each new booking's confirmation carries the link again').

then.description: A copy is a customer's copy of a message about a booking, in that booking's thread (RULES 4.1).

sendEmail.response.title: SendEmailResponse
sendEmail.response.description: Resend accepted the email (02-contracts K-12: 'returns the provider's message id'). Its id goes to the part through K-05 markPart sent (K-07 providerMessageId), and its receipts name it (K-06 status.messageId), so they find the part. Accepted is not delivered: delivery comes later as a K-06 delivered receipt (arch 02 line 127). A repeat under the same key within 24 hours answers this same id (README 'Spike findings').

providerMessageId.description: Resend's id for the email (its response's id).

sendEmail.errors.title: SendEmailErrors
sendEmail.errors.description: Resend refused or failed the email. The kind tells the dispatcher what K-07's rules do: rateLimited, a 429 rate_limit_exceeded, tried again after its retry-after (arch 10 line 540; K-07 rule 6); quotaReached, a 429 daily or monthly quota (the daily one resets at midnight UTC), which no try within the 15 minutes clears, so the row fails and the next way follows (K-07 rule 5; J-14: Free's 100 emails a day); refused, any other 4xx, such as a validation error, an unverified domain, a key problem or a key reused with another email, never tried again as it was (K-07 rule 5's next way); transient, a 5xx, a 409 for the same key still in progress, a timeout or a network error, tried again under K-07's rules (arch 02 line 125). The code is Resend's error name, as text (K-04 outbox_parts.error_code).

httpStatus.description: The HTTP status Resend answered with; null when no answer came (a timeout or a network error).

code.description: Resend's error name, such as rate_limit_exceeded, daily_quota_exceeded or validation_error; null when it gave none.

reason.description: What failed, in Resend's words or the adapter's, for the team console's failed rows (C-194). Never a key, an address or the email's words.

retryAfterSeconds.description: For rateLimited: the wait Resend gave (its retry-after header), which K-07 stores as the claim's nextTryNotBefore; null when it gave none, and for every other kind (arch 10 line 540).

kind.description: The statuses and names each kind is read from (README 'Outcomes of a send').

verifyWebhook.request.title: EmailVerifyWebhookRequest
verifyWebhook.request.description: One webhook as the gateway (C-044) received it from Resend, before any parsing. Resend signs its webhooks through Svix: the adapter reads the svix-id, svix-timestamp and svix-signature headers into these fields (README 'Spike findings').

webhookId.description: The svix-id header: the webhook's id, the same on every retry of it, so it is the event id duplicates are dropped by (K-06 eventId; arch 02 line 109).

timestamp.description: The svix-timestamp header as sent, whole seconds since 1970, which must lie within 300 s of receivedAt (the window arch 02 line 109 gives Linq's webhooks; Svix's own libraries reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes off). Kept as text, so a header that is not whole seconds is refused rather than read.

signature.description: The svix-signature header exactly as sent: one or more 'v1,<base64>' separated by spaces. Empty when the header is missing.

raw.description: The body exactly as received, byte for byte as text; the signature covers '<webhookId>.<timestamp>.<raw>'. Never parsed before the signature passes.

receivedAt.description: When the gateway received it (K-06 receivedAt), the 'now' the 300 s window is measured from.

traceId.description: The trace id the gateway opened at receipt (K-08 v1; arch 10 line 548); the parsed event carries it as K-06 traceId.

failureCode.title: EmailFailureCode
failureCode.description: How an email failed, as the K-06 failure code of an email's failed receipt (K-06 failure.code: 'K-11, K-12 list them'): bouncePermanent, Resend's email.bounced with bounce type Permanent (the address does not take mail); bounceTemporary, email.bounced with any other bounce type; suppressed, email.suppressed (Resend did not send it: the address is on the suppression list); notSent, email.failed (it could not be sent, such as reached_daily_quota). Each is a failure that starts the channel fallback (02-contracts K-12 'failed or bounced (the channel fallback)'; arch 02 line 125).

receiptEvent.title: EmailReceiptEvent
receiptEvent.description: A delivery event for one of Rosie's emails as one K-06 v1 event, its provider email: delivered (Resend's email.delivered, which arms the question's clock: arch 02 line 127) or failed (a bounce, a suppression or a failure to send, the channel fallback: 02-contracts K-12). K-06 gives the rest: the handle the email went to, service email, status.messageId Resend's email id, which sendEmail returned, and status.at when Resend reported it.

verifyWebhook.response.title: EmailVerifyWebhookResponse
verifyWebhook.response.description: The signature passed. event: a delivery event parsed into one K-06 event, with the email's Message-ID beside it (rfcMessageId), which the gateway seals and hands to the dispatcher and clock arming, then answers 200 (arch 02 lines 109, 127); a known event id also gets 200 and is dropped, and a failed write gets 503 so Resend retries. reply: Resend's email.received, which carries only a reply's metadata, so the gateway reads the reply with readReply before it writes anything and answers after that (README 'Inbound replies'). ignored: a signed event of a type Rosie does not use (README default 10), answered 200 and dropped.

httpStatus.description: What the gateway answers once the event is written (arch 02 line 109).

rfcMessageId.description: The Message-ID of Rosie's email the receipt reports on (Resend's message_id), which later emails in the booking's thread name in In-Reply-To and References; null when Resend gives none (email.suppressed and email.failed: the email never went). K-06 v1 has no field for it, so it travels beside the event, never in it.

if.description: An email that never went has no Message-ID (README 'Spike findings').

eventId.description: The event id the reply's K-06 event will carry, the webhook id; the gateway drops a known one with 200 before reading (arch 02 line 109).

receivedEmailId.description: Resend's id for the received email, which readReply reads it by.

replyAddress.description: The address on Rosie's receiving domain it was sent to: the first of to, cc and received_for there (README default 13). The booking's own reply address picks the booking and thread (02-contracts K-12; RULES 4.1; K-04 threads.reply_address), so the gateway can tell a booking's reply from other mail before reading it.

eventType.description: Resend's event type, for the log (README 'Spike findings' lists them).

verifyWebhook.errors.title: EmailVerifyWebhookErrors
verifyWebhook.errors.description: The webhook is rejected: the gateway answers 401 and drops it, and it never becomes an event (arch 02 line 109: 'Bad signature: 401, dropped'). badTimestamp: the svix-timestamp header is not whole seconds; staleTimestamp: it lies more than 300 s from receivedAt; badSignature: no signature in the header matches. The reason is a label only: never the key, the body or the signature (rule 7).

readReply.request.title: ReadReplyRequest
readReply.request.description: Read one inbound reply that verifyWebhook announced (02-contracts K-12 'Inbound replies'). Resend's email.received webhook carries only metadata, so the adapter reads the email (its text, headers, attachments and sender check) from Resend's receiving API (README 'Spike findings').

eventId.description: The webhook id verifyWebhook gave as eventId: the K-06 event's eventId.

receivedEmailId.description: Resend's id for the received email (verifyWebhook receivedEmailId).

receivedAt.description: When the gateway received the webhook (K-06 receivedAt).

traceId.description: The trace id the gateway opened at receipt (K-06 traceId; K-08).

replyEvent.title: EmailReplyEvent
replyEvent.description: An inbound reply as one K-06 v1 event, its provider email and kind text (02-contracts K-12: 'turned into K-06 events for the handle's actor'): from is the handle; to, the booking's reply address, is email.replyAddress, which picks the booking and thread; the subject is email.subject; the text is the body; the attachments are the event's (K-13 turns each id into a file reference); the sender check is email.senderCheck (RULES 6.1). A reply threads under no message in v1 (threadedReplyTo null: its reply address already names its thread; README default 18).

readReply.response.title: ReadReplyResponse
readReply.response.description: The reply is read. event: one K-06 text event, which the gateway seals and writes to the handle's actor, then answers the webhook 200 (arch 02 line 109). ignored: an automatic reply, such as an out-of-office note (its Auto-Submitted header is other than 'no': RFC 3834), which is answered 200 and dropped, so no loop of automatic emails starts (README default 17).

readReply.errors.title: ReadReplyErrors
readReply.errors.description: The reply could not be read. transient: a 5xx, a timeout, a network error, or a key that cannot read received email (Resend's restricted_api_key for a send-only key: README open gap 1): the gateway answers the webhook 503, so Resend retries it (arch 02 line 109: 'Write fails: 503, and the provider retries'). unreadable: Resend has no such email, or keeps none of its content (not_found, email_above_quota): answered 200 and dropped, and the team console shows it (C-194). The code is Resend's error name, as text.

httpStatus.description: What the gateway answers the webhook: 503 for transient, 200 for unreadable.

code.description: Resend's error name; null when it gave none.

reason.description: What failed, in Resend's words or the adapter's; never a key, an address or the email's words.

doubleWebhook.request.title: EmailDoubleWebhookRequest
doubleWebhook.request.description: Ask the email double (C-213's double; test code only) for a signed webhook in Resend's form that carries one event: a faked delivered or bounce receipt for an email it recorded, or a faked inbound reply (02-contracts K-12 'The double's test hooks': 'fakes delivered and bounce events and inbound replies'; BP 9.4). For a reply the double also keeps the reply, so readReply on the id it gives answers the request's event with the gateway's own receivedAt and traceId.

event.description: The K-06 v1 event the gateway must get back: from verifyWebhook for a receipt, from readReply for a reply, given the same receivedAt and traceId; its provider is email.

rfcMessageId.description: For a delivered or bounced receipt, the Message-ID the webhook reports, which verifyWebhook gives back beside the event; else null.

if.description: A reply's own Message-ID is its event's messageId; nothing travels beside it.

doubleWebhook.response.title: EmailDoubleWebhookResponse
doubleWebhook.response.description: The signed webhook, ready for the gateway: verifyWebhook on it, inside the 300 s window, gives back the request's receipt and rfcMessageId, or for a reply the reply outcome naming receivedEmailId, on which readReply gives back the request's event (the contract test's round trip). Signed with the test environment's webhook secret, never Resend's (rule 7).

receivedEmailId.description: For a reply, the double's id for the reply it keeps for readReply; null for a receipt.

doubleSentEmails.request.title: DoubleSentEmailsRequest
doubleSentEmails.request.description: Ask the email double (test code only) for the emails it recorded, so the staging test-phone page can show them (02-contracts K-12: 'records each email ... and shows its output on the test-phone page'; BP 9.4; C-205), such as a confirmation's chat link for a tester to send its ready text.

to.description: Only the emails to this address; null for every email recorded.

doubleSentEmails.response.title: DoubleSentEmailsResponse
doubleSentEmails.response.description: The emails the double accepted, oldest first, each as its sendEmail request with the id the double gave it. A repeat under one key is recorded once, as Resend sends it once.

providerMessageId.description: The id the double answered with (sendEmail.response providerMessageId).
